info.title: Rhizolog
info.description:
A wiki over a directory of markdown files. Markdown on disk is the source of truth; the search index is derived from it and can be rebuilt at any time.

Page content is served as raw markdown by default — pass `render=true` to also receive rendered HTML.

Slugs may contain `/` (`notes/rust/async`), so the page path segment spans the rest of the URL.

Every error, whatever the status, has the shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Branch on `code`; it is stable. `message` is prose.

get.summary:
Report that the server is running, which wiki it is serving, and how fresh
its index is.
Both directions of a page's links.
get.description:
The slug does not have to name a page that exists: asking about a wanted
page returns what already points at it, which is what you want to see before
deciding whether to write it.

Both directions come back together because that is how they are used — a
page view shows its links and its backlinks at once, and one round trip
beats two.

200.description: Links into and out of the page

post.summary: Move a page to a new slug.
post.description:
Inbound links are left as they are. They become wanted pages, so a move
shows up in the wiki's stats rather than rotting quietly.

200.description: The page at its new slug

400.description: One of the slugs is not valid

404.description: No page at the source slug

409.description: A page already exists at the destination

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Return only pages carrying this tag.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description:
Return only pages at or under this slug path.

`notes/rust` matches the page `notes/rust` and everything beneath it.
It stops at the separator, so `notes/rustlings` is a different
directory and does not match. Matching is case-sensitive.

parameters.name: segment
parameters.description:
Return only pages sitting in a directory of this name, wherever in the
wiki that directory is.

`rust` matches `notes/rust/async` and `code/rust/traits` alike — the
flat reading of a slug, which is why it behaves like `tag` rather than
like `prefix`. A page's own name is not a directory it sits in, so
`async` does not match `notes/rust/async`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of the summary fields to return, for cheap
listings. Naming an unknown field is refused, and the error lists the
ones that would have worked.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many matches to skip. Pair it with `total` in the response.

400.description: Unknown field, sort key, or order

post.summary: Create a page. Fails if one already exists at that slug.

409.description: A page already exists at that slug

parameters.name: render
parameters.description:
Also return the body rendered to HTML, in an `html` field. The markdown
is still returned either way.

422.description: The page exists but could not be parsed

put.summary: Create or wholly replace a page.

patch.summary: Update some of a page, leaving the rest alone.

put.description:
Idempotent: pinning a page that is already pinned succeeds and leaves its
position alone, so a client does not have to check first.

409.description: The pin limit is already reached

delete.description:
Unpinning something that was not pinned is a `404`, matching `DELETE` on a
page: an operation that did nothing is worth knowing about. The page itself
is untouched — this removes the shortcut, not the wiki entry.

post.summary: Rebuild the search index from the wiki directory.
post.description:
The index holds nothing that is not already on disk, so this is always safe
and never loses anything. It is the escape hatch for the one case
incremental scanning can miss: an edit that leaves both mtime and size
unchanged.

post.summary: Render markdown to HTML without storing it.
post.description:
`GET /api/pages/{slug}?render=true` renders what is *saved*, which is no use
to an editor showing an unsaved draft. This renders whatever it is handed,
through the same renderer, so a preview cannot disagree with what the page
will look like once written. Rendering in the client instead would mean a
second markdown implementation that does not know about wikilinks, and it
would be wrong in exactly the places this wiki cares about.

Nothing is read or written, so this is safe to call on every keystroke.

400.description: The request body is not valid

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Terms to search for. Matched literally and combined with AND; a
trailing `*` on a term searches by prefix. Punctuation is safe to
include — it is never interpreted as query syntax.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many matches to skip. Pair it with `total` in the response.

get.description:
Orphans and wanted pages are the two most useful numbers here, and they are
two sides of the same thing: pages nothing reaches, and reaches with nothing
at the end. A wiki that branches chaotically accumulates both.

get.summary: Every tag in the wiki, with page counts.

# Async in Rust

Futures are lazy. See [[notes/rust/pinning]].

slug.description: Where the page will live. `409` if something is already there.

tags.description:
Free-form; tags are whatever you have used elsewhere. `GET /api/tags`
lists the ones already in play.

title.description:
Optional. Without it the title falls back to the body's first heading,
then to the slug.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for what went wrong.

details.description:
Context for correcting the request, when there is any. Where something
was refused for being outside a fixed set, this names the values that
would have worked.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Prose; do not branch on it.

error.description:
Every failure has this shape, whatever the status. Branch on
`error.code`.

last_indexed.description:
When the index was last reconciled with the wiki directory. Null if it
has not been scanned yet.

status.description: Always `"ok"` — a response at all is the liveness signal.

wiki_root.description: Absolute path of the wiki directory being served.

display.description: What the link says, when that differs from the target.

kind.description: `wiki` or `internal`. A page cannot be reached by an external link.

internal.description: Links pointing at pages, whether or not those pages exist.

wanted.description: Internal links whose target has not been written yet.

referrers.description: How many pages link to it.

from.description: The page to move. `404` if there is nothing there.

to.description: Where it goes. `409` if that slug is taken.

display.description: The link's text, when it says something other than the target.

kind.description:
`wiki` (`[[slug]]`), `internal` (a markdown link to a page), or
`external`.

resolved.description:
Whether this points at a page that exists. A `false` here is not an
error — it is a wanted page.

target.description: A slug for `wiki` and `internal` links, a URL for `external` ones.

title.description: Title of the target page, when it exists.

exists.description: Whether the page itself exists. Links can point at pages that do not.

inbound.description: Pages that link here — the backlinks.

outbound.description: Links this page makes, in document order, deduplicated per kind.

slug.description: The slug that was asked about.

limit.description: The limit that was applied, after clamping.

pages.description:
Bodies are never included here. When `fields` is given, each entry
carries only the requested subset of these keys.

total.description: Total matching pages, not the number returned.

created.description: When the page was first written, falling back to the file's mtime.

size.description: Size of the page's file on disk, in bytes.

tags.description: The page's tags, in the order the frontmatter lists them.

title.description:
The page's effective title: its frontmatter `title`, or failing that the
body's first heading, or failing that the slug.

content.description:
The page body as markdown, without its frontmatter. Title and tags are
returned as fields above rather than left in the text, so an editor
never has to reserialise YAML to change one of them.

# Async in Rust

Futures are lazy. See [[notes/rust/pinning]].

created.description:
When the page was first written. Falls back to the file's mtime for
pages written by hand, which never carried the field.

html.description:
The body rendered to HTML. Present only when `render=true` was asked
for.

Raw HTML in the source is dropped rather than passed through — the
markup does not appear in the output at all, escaped or otherwise. Links
to pages come back as browsable `/pages/...` URLs.

Futures are lazy. See notes/rust/pinning.

size.description: Size of the page's file on disk, in bytes.

tags.description: The page's tags, in the order the frontmatter lists them.

title.description:
The page's effective title: its frontmatter `title`, or failing that the
body's first heading, or failing that the slug.

title_derived.description:
Whether `title` was derived rather than stored — from the body's first
heading, or failing that the slug.

This is what makes read-modify-write safe. Send a derived title back and
it stops being derived: it is written into the frontmatter, and the
heading it came from can never update it again. A client editing a page
should send `null` for the title while this is true, and the editor in
the dashboard leaves its title field empty for exactly that reason.

PatchPage.description: A partial update. Omitted fields are left alone.

content.description: Replaces the whole body when present.
content.example:
# Async in Rust

Futures are lazy. See [[notes/rust/pinning]].

tags.description: Replaces the whole tag list when present.

title.description:
Omit to leave the title unchanged; send `null` to clear it and fall
back to the heading or slug.

exists.description:
Whether a page still exists at this slug.

A pin can outlive its page — a file removed or renamed outside Rhizolog
leaves one behind. That is reported rather than cleaned up silently, so
the pin can be removed deliberately.

pinned_at.description: When it was pinned. Pinning an already-pinned page does not change this.

title.description: The pinned page's title, falling back to the slug when no page is there.

limit.description:
How many pins there may be in total, so a client can say why a pin was
refused before it tries.

pins.description:
Oldest pin first. The order is stable: pinning something new appends to
it and re-pinning moves nothing.

failed.description: Pages on disk that could not be read, and so are not searchable.

indexed.description: Pages read and written to the index.

removed.description: Pages dropped because they are no longer on disk.

RenderRequest.description: Markdown to render, with the context its links need.

oneOf.description:
The slug this content is, or would be, saved at.

It matters only for relative markdown links: `[traits](traits.md)` names
a different page depending on where it is written. Omit it and relative
links resolve from the wiki root. Wikilinks are unaffected — they are
always absolute.

The rendered body. Raw HTML in the source is dropped rather than passed
through, and links to pages come back as browsable `/pages/...` URLs.

ReplacePage.description: A whole page. Every field is replaced, including the ones left out.

content.description: Markdown body, without frontmatter. Omitting this empties the page.
content.example:
# Async in Rust

Futures are lazy. See [[notes/rust/pinning]].

tags.description: Omitting this clears the page's tags. Use `PATCH` to leave them alone.

title.description:
Send `null` to let the title follow the body's first heading. Sending a
title the server derived is what freezes it — see `title_derived`.

count.description:
Calls since the wiki was created. Counts survive restarts; they live in
the durable half of the index, not the rebuildable half.

route.description: The route template, as the OpenAPI document spells it.

score.description: Relevance. Higher is better; comparable only within one result set.

snippet.description:
An excerpt of the body with matched terms wrapped in `<mark>`. This is
here so a caller can judge which hits are worth fetching without
pulling every body.

Only the marks are markup: the text around them is the page body
verbatim and is **not** escaped, so a client rendering this as HTML
would be rendering whatever the page contains.

tags.description: Its tags, so a caller can filter results without fetching each page.

limit.description: The limit that was applied, after clamping.

total.description: Total matches, not the number returned.

Slug.description:
A page's identifier: its path under the wiki root, `/`-separated, without the `.md` extension. `notes/rust/async.md` is `notes/rust/async`.

Slugs must not begin or end with `/`, contain an empty segment, `.`, `..`, a backslash, or any of `< > : " | ? *`. No segment may begin or end with a dot or whitespace, or be a reserved Windows device name such as `CON` or `LPT1` — a wiki written on one operating system stays valid on the other.

A rejected slug comes back as a `400` whose `details.rule` names which of these was broken.

api_usage.description: API calls per route since the wiki was created, busiest first.

last_indexed.description: When the index was last reconciled with the wiki directory.

links.description: Link counts, split by where they point.

wanted_count.description: Distinct slugs that are linked to but do not exist.

pages.description: How many pages carry this tag.

tag.description: The tag, exactly as pages spell it. Tags are not normalised.

referrers.description: How many pages link to it — how badly it is wanted.

slug.description: The slug that is linked to but does not exist.
